newsitem.title: JAPAN: Five Japan firms to invest in Australia coal mine.
newsitem.headline: Five Japan firms to invest in Australia coal mine.

text.p: Five Japanese companies have decided to acquire stakes in an Australian coal mine as part of efforts to secure stable supplies, company spokesmen said on Wednesday.

Tomen Corp, Nittetsu Shoji Co, Sumikin Bussan Kaisha Ltd, Kokan Mining Co Ltd and Shinsho Corp plan to buy a combined seven percent share in the Moranbah-North mine in Queensland from Shell Coal Australia Ltd, they said.
Last October, Nippon Steel Corp agreed to buy a five-percent stake in the Moranbah-North mine.

The seven percent stake will be divided between the five Japanese firms as follows: Tomen 3.75 percent, Nittetsu Shoji 1.25 percent, Sumikin Bussan Kaisha one percent, Kokan Mining 0.5 percent and Shinsho Corp 0.5 percent, their spokesmen said.
Shell Coal Australia will own the remaining 88 percent.
Output at the Moranbah-North mine, which will start production in 1998, is expected to reach 3.8 million tonnes a year by 2001, the spokesmen said.
